item.title: High costs, higher risks: Can the Philippines power its data centre hub ambitions?
item.description: The Philippines’ ambition to become a data centre hub is running up against high electricity prices and a coal-heavy grid.

item.title: Singapore university trials carbon-labelled meals on campus menus
item.description: The carbon footprint of meals is to be displayed on select menus at the National University of Singapore. But convenience-conscious students are sceptical that the initiative will inspire environmentally-friendly dining.

item.title: Bangkok, Vientiane choke as hazardous haze pushes air pollution beyond health limits
item.description: PM2.5 levels in Thailand’s capital and Laos’ largest city climb to unhealthy and hazardous ranges, prompting emergency measures and renewed calls for regional action on seasonal haze.

item.title: The AI we need for sustainable infrastructure
item.description: Even as governments pour trillions of dollars into roads, power grids, data centers, water systems, and housing, the construction industry has yet to leverage the efficiency gains that AI and digitalisation have to offer.

item.title: Australian insurers declare catastrophe as Victoria bushfire losses mount, climate risks intensify
item.description: Claims surge as insurers warn extreme fires highlight escalating climate risk. More than 400,000 hectares of bushland and farmland have burned – more than five times the size of Singapore.

item.title: How is the Chinese public engaging in climate adaptation?
item.description: While government message boards and NGOs are growing in importance, community self-organising remains crucial.

item.title: How the Philippines can leverage its Asean chairship to meet climate goals
item.description: Finalising ambitious climate targets, being self-reliant for climate funding and striving to uphold human rights aspects of critical minerals are ways the new Asean chair can steer the region to meet low carbon ambitions.

item.title: How data centres can avoid becoming the next coal mines
item.description: The resistance to AI will come from the social disruption it will bring – and data centres will be where that backlash lands first. Investors in AI must ensure that its benefits are shared, harm is reduced, and value created locally.

item.title: World Bank's IFC appoints Asia Pacific regional vice president
item.description: Indian national Sarvesh Suri moves into the Singapore-based role, replacing Riccardo Puliti, who has moved to Dubai to run IFC's Middle East and Central Asia division.

item.title: What chief sustainability officers fear in 2026
item.description: From dwindling influence to grappling with policy delay, Eco-Business asked Asia's sustainability leaders what is likely to keep them awake at night in the year of the horse.
